daily_brief: The United States launched extensive retaliatory strikes against Iran overnight, hitting dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets including military command centers, missile facilities, and coastal defense sites [France 24, Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail, The Hindu]. Iranian state media reported three civilian deaths, including a two-year-old child, on Qeshm Island [France 24, Al Jazeera]. The escalation follows Iran's missile attack on US bases in Jordan, though Pakistan confirmed negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain ongoing [France 24]. In Europe, firefighters continue battling massive wildfires across southern regions, with French authorities allowing 84,000 evacuees to return home while over 220,000 were displaced since the blaze began [France 24, RFI]. The EU's crisis management chief called for increased prevention funding as climate change intensifies fire risks [RFI]. Meanwhile, Russia struck Ukraine with missiles reaching as far as Lviv near the Polish border, killing at least 13 people and forcing Poland to scramble fighter jets [Globe and Mail]. The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady despite persistent inflation [Le Monde, Financial Times], while a magnitude 7.1 earthquake in Japan's Kumamoto region has killed at least 23 people, disrupting supply chains for automakers including Nissan and Daihatsu [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia].

top_stories.headline: US Launches Two-Hour Strike Campaign Against Iran, Killing Three Civilians Including Child
bullets: US Central Command struck dozens of Iranian Revolutionary Guard targets over two hours, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, and coastal defense sites
Iranian state media reported three deaths on Qeshm Island, including a two-year-old child, with two other children injured in what authorities described as a strike on a residential building
The strikes were in retaliation for Iran's missile attack on US bases in Jordan; Iran's Revolutionary Guards vowed to 'punish the aggressor'
Pakistan confirmed US-Iran negotiations remain ongoing despite the renewed fighting, particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz and de-escalation

top_stories.headline: Southern Europe Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations as EU Calls for Prevention Investment
bullets: French authorities authorized 84,000 evacuees to return home after a wildfire in the Gironde department burned an area four times the size of Paris
More than 220,000 people were forced to flee since the blaze began; 2,200 firefighters and 20 aircraft remain mobilized
Turkey is battling 115 active fires across tourist regions including Antalya; a new fire in Spain near the Portuguese border forced 600 more evacuations
EU Crisis Management Commissioner Hadja Lahbib called for greater investment in wildfire prevention, forest management, and public education as climate change accelerates

top_stories.headline: Russian Missile Strikes Kill 13 Across Ukraine, Force Poland to Scramble Jets
bullets: Russian air strikes killed at least 13 people across Ukraine, including six in Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih where two girls aged 5 and 12 died
Strikes reached Lviv near the Polish border, damaging two apartment buildings and injuring 26 people; Poland scrambled fighter jets to secure airspace
The attacks coincided with Zelensky's return from Washington, where Trump agreed to provide Ukraine licenses for Patriot missile production
Air raid alerts sounded across most Ukrainian regions; emergency workers continue searching rubble with death toll expected to rise

top_stories.headline: Japan Earthquake Death Toll Reaches 23 as Automakers Face Supply Chain Disruptions
bullets: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island Tuesday, killing at least 23 people with 63 injured
The most serious damage occurred at Aeon Mall shopping center in Kashima, where an explosion occurred after the quake while thousands were evacuating
Nissan and Daihatsu production remains halted due to the earthquake's impact on regional supply chains
Thousands remain in evacuation centers; some homes lack water and electricity, and older Japanese-style housing proved particularly vulnerable

top_stories.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Despite Elevated Inflation, Borrowing Costs Hit 19-Year High
bullets: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged despite persistently high inflation
US borrowing costs have reached their highest level in 19 years
The decision comes amid ongoing debate about the Fed's approach to managing inflation while avoiding recession
Market analysts are divided on whether the Fed's patience will prove justified or lead to further price pressures
